subject: Civil Engineering
title: Embankment Dams
description: A quick, practical guide to Embankment Dams.

hook.text: The tallest dams in the world are mounds of earth and rock — not concrete.

buildup.text: Embankment dams pile compacted soil and rock in layers — creating a massive triangular fill.

discovery.text: A clay core or geomembrane at the center stops water from seeping through the fill.

twist.text: They suit wide valleys where concrete dams would be impractical — and can use local materials.

climax.text: The Tarbela Dam in Pakistan — one of the largest embankment dams — holds back the Indus.

punchline.text: Pile enough earth and rock, seal the core, and a mountain becomes a dam.

quiz.question: What prevents water from seeping through an embankment dam?
options: The sheer weight of the rock and soil compresses out all voids
A clay core or geomembrane at the center acts as a waterproof barrier
Water naturally flows around the dam instead of through it
